{{Short description|Generalization of natural transformations}}<!-- <-- OK now? cited 2 sources -->
In [[mathematics]], specifically in [[category theory]], an '''extranatural transformation'''<ref name="kelly">[[Samuel Eilenberg|Eilenberg]] and [[Max Kelly|Kelly]], A generalization of the functorial calculus, J. Algebra 3 366–375 (1966)</ref> is a generalization of the notion of [[natural transformation]].

==Definition==
Let <math>F:A\times B^\mathrm{op}\times B\rightarrow D</math> and <math> G:A\times C^\mathrm{op}\times C\rightarrow D </math> be two [[functor]]s of categories.
A family <math>\eta (a,b,c):F(a,b,b)\rightarrow G(a,c,c)</math> is said to be '''natural in''' ''a'' '''and extranatural in''' ''b'' '''and''' ''c'' if the following holds:
*<math>\eta(-,b,c)</math> is a natural transformation (in the usual sense).
* (extranaturality in ''b'') <math>\forall (g:b\rightarrow b^\prime)\in \mathrm{Mor}\, B</math>, <math>\forall a\in A</math>, <math>\forall c\in C</math> the following [[commutative diagram|diagram commutes]]

:: <math>\begin{matrix}
F(a,b',b) & \xrightarrow{F(1,1,g)} & F(a,b',b') \\
_{F(1,g,1)}\downarrow\qquad & & _{\eta(a,b',c)}\downarrow\qquad \\
F(a,b,b) & \xrightarrow{\eta(a,b,c)} & G(a,c,c)
\end{matrix}</math>

* (extranaturality in ''c'') <math>\forall (h:c\rightarrow c^\prime)\in \mathrm{Mor}\, C</math>, <math>\forall a\in A</math>, <math>\forall b\in B</math> the following diagram commutes

:: <math>\begin{matrix}
F(a,b,b) & \xrightarrow{\eta(a,b,c')} & G(a,c',c') \\
_{\eta(a,b,c)}\downarrow\qquad & & _{G(1,h,1)}\downarrow\qquad \\
G(a,c,c) & \xrightarrow{G(1,1,h)} & G(a,c,c')
\end{matrix}</math>

== Properties ==
Extranatural transformations can be used to define wedges and thereby [[End (category theory)|ends]]<ref name="cofriend">Fosco Loregian, ''This is the (co)end, my only (co)friend'', arXiv preprint [https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.02503]</ref> (dually co-wedges and co-ends), by setting <math>F</math> (dually <math>G</math>) constant.

Extranatural transformations can be defined in terms of [[dinatural transformation]]s, of which they are a special case.<ref name="cofriend"/>
